display_name: Howard Park Leston Shiraz, Margaret River
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Margaret River's red gravelly loams concentrate Shiraz flavors into black plum and green peppercorn in Howard Park Leston, sidestepping Barossa's ripe jam. The 2016 vintage earned 89 points for its mint lift after airing out initial reductiveness. This stands out in a region better known for Cabernet.",
  "wine_summary": "Howard Park sources Leston Shiraz from Margaret River's 2,137 km² GI, where maritime winds tame Shiraz power into balanced reds. The producer builds reputation through site-specific wines, with bronzes at TEXSOM for 2003 and 2015 vintages proving consistency. Terroir here delivers pepper and mint over sheer fruit weight, setting it apart from eastern Australia's heat-driven styles.",
  "terroir_expression": "Red gravelly loam and loamy gravel over clay in Margaret River provide drainage and depth, yielding structured tannins and concentrated black fruits that avoid flab. Deep infertile sands stress vines for intensity, while Forest Grove ironstone adds mineral edge to the glass. Indian Ocean breezes bring cool nights and diurnal swings, preserving green peppercorn snap and eucalyptus mint in the 89-point NV.",
  "vinification_summary": "Fermentation likely uses partial closure to build the noted reductiveness—sulfur aromas from low-oxygen conditions that disperse with air, revealing plum and berry core. Oak aging integrates green peppercorn spice without overpowering site notes. These choices preserve Margaret River freshness in a grape that elsewhere turns heavy.",
  "food_pairing": "Grilled kangaroo skewers with pepper bush rub: peppercorn notes echo the wine's spice while tannins handle red meat char. Nashville hot chicken: mint cools heat, fruit cuts fried fat. Rack of lamb persillade: herbal lift matches rosemary, structure binds garlic butter. Steak frites au poivre: green pepper aligns with sauce, body stands to beef. Wood-fired pizza with spicy salami: acidity slices cheese, plum bolsters tomato.",
  "comparable_wines": "Cape Mentelle Margaret River Shiraz — shared gravel soils drive similar black fruit and pepper structure. Vasse Felix Margaret River Shiraz — ocean-cooled freshness mirrors the mint and balance. d'Arenberg The Footbolt Shiraz — McLaren Vale gravel counterpart with extra tannin grip.",
  "style_profile": "Full-bodied dry Shiraz with firm tannins and green peppercorn lift",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Open 2016 and 2015 now after decanting; 2012 holds to 2028. Store at 55°F in dark, vibration-free conditions.",
  "value_assessment": "$25-35 AUD. Cape Mentelle Shiraz ($30) and Vasse Felix ($35) compete directly. Buy for the terroir clarity that outpunches price.",
  "market_position": "Margaret River fans and Aussie steakhouse lists stock this for everyday reds with upside. Retail in US imports targets barbecue crowds over collectors. Casual drinkers grab it for value in 750ml bottles.",
  "insider_take": "Skip if you chase Barossa bombast—this trades heft for peppery precision that rewards patient swirling. The real win hides under initial closure, so decant every time. Wallcliffe subregion fans will hoard older vintages like 2003.",
  "aging_potential_years": 12,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 3,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 15,
